_meta.indication: HALAVEN is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic breast cancer who have previously received at least two chemotherapeutic regimens for the treatment of metastatic disease, with prior therapy that included an anthracycline and a taxane.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized (2:1), active-controlled, multicenter trial of eribulin versus treatment of physician's choice (TPC)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received two to five prior chemotherapy regimens, including an anthracycline and a taxane
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint, comparing eribulin-treated patients with those treated with treatment of physician's choice (TPC)
pivotal_trials.result: Median OS 13.1 months (eribulin) vs 10.6 months (control); HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.66, 0.99); p=0.041. ORR 11.2% vs 3.9% (p=0.0006).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥25%) were neutropenia, anemia, asthenia/fatigue, alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, nausea, and constipation. Neutropenia all-grades 82% (vs 53% control); Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy 8%. Most serious adverse reactions were febrile neutropenia (4%) and neutropenia (2%); peripheral neuropathy was the most common cause of discontinuation (5%).
target_moa: Eribulin is a non-taxane microtubule dynamics inhibitor that inhibits tubulin polymerization and microtubule growth (but not shortening), interfering with mitotic spindle formation and causing G2/M cell cycle arrest and block in the prometaphase portion of mitosis.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic analogue of halichondrin B)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; three ODAC members were consulted individually (two physicians and a patient advocate) and considered the risk:benefit positive, supporting approval.

description.text: Added indication for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma after prior anthracycline-containing regimen

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma who have received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use subsection with results from pediatric clinical studies conducted under an amended Written Request

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the Halaven (eribulin mesylate) Prescribing Information (PI) updating Section 8, Use in Specific Populations, Subsection 8.4, Pediatric Use, to include results from pediatric clinical studies conducted in accordance with the amended Written Request issued on November 10, 2021. basis.text: Fast Track designation granted August 21, 2007 for locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer refractory to or relapsed after standard therapy, based on demonstration of antitumor activity.

citations.quote: On Aug 21, 2007, FDA granted eribulin Fast Track designation for the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer refractory to or relapsed after treatment with standard therapy based on antitumor activity based on demonstration of antitumor activity.

basis.text: The application was assigned priority review on May 28, 2010.

citations.quote: On March 30, 2010, Eisai submitted NDA 201-532. The application was assigned priority review on May 28, 2010 and filed on June 11, 2010, with an action goal date of September 30, 2010. On August 25, 2010, FDA notified Eisai that the review had been extended by 3 months based on submission of a major amendment, resulting in a new action date of December 30, 2010.

summary.text: Eisai sought and received regular (full) approval for Halaven based on a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival in a single Phase 3 trial (EMBRACE/Study 305). The product had Fast Track designation (granted August 21, 2007) and the application received priority review (May 28, 2010); it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Eisai, Inc. sought regular approval for Halaven Injection (eribulin mesylate) for (b) (4) with metastatic breast cancer based on demonstration of a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival (OS) in a single trial.

On Aug 21, 2007, FDA granted eribulin Fast Track designation for the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer refractory to or relapsed after treatment with standard therapy based on antitumor activity based on demonstration of antitumor activity.
The application was assigned priority review on May 28, 2010 and filed on June 11, 2010, with an action goal date of September 30, 2010.

requirement.text: PMR 1689-1: Conduct a dedicated clinical trial assessing the safety and pharmacokinetics of Halaven in subjects with normal renal function and subjects with severe renal impairment.

citations.quote: To conduct a dedicated clinical trial assessing the safety and pharmacokinetics of Halaven, in accordance with FDA Guidance for Industry: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function - Study Design, Data Analysis and Impact on Dosing and Labeling. The trial design should include subjects with normal renal function and subjects with severe renal impairment.

requirement.text: PMC 1689-2: Submit a final report with updated overall survival results after 95% of patient deaths (724 deaths in 762 enrolled patients) for trial E7389-G000-305.

citations.quote: To submit a final report that includes updated results for overall survival after 95% of patient deaths have occurred (724 deaths in 762 enrolled patients) for trial E7389-G000-305, “A Phase 3 Open Label, Randomized Parallel Two-Arm Multi-Center Study of E7389 versus ‘Treatment of Physician’s Choice’ in Patients with Locally Recurrent or Metastatic Breast Cancer, Previously Treated with At Least Two and a Maximum of Five Prior Chemotherapy Regimens, Including an Anthracycline and a Taxane”. The final report should also include the primary and derived datasets and analysis programs used to generate the overall survival results reported.

requirement.text: PMC 1689-3: Submit a final report for the ongoing trial E7389-G000-301 (eribulin versus capecitabine), including a subset analysis of overall survival in patients who progressed on a taxane or other microtubule inhibiting agent.

citations.quote: To submit a final report for the ongoing trial, E7389-G000-301, "A Phase III Open Label, Randomized Two-Parallel-Arm Multicenter Study of E7389 versus Capecitabine in Patients with Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer Previously Treated with Anthracyclines and Taxanes." This report will include a subset analysis of overall survival in patients that progressed while on treatment with a taxane or other microtubule inhibiting agent, in addition to all protocol-specified analyses.
